title: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of antithrombotic therapy for atrial fibrillation
author: Xiaoxuan Gong1*
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iijcccn

steps.title: Search Databases for Records
steps.instruction: Independently search PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central from the earliest possible date until March 2017 using specific keywords.

substeps.instruction: Use search keywords: (“atrial fibrillation” or “AF”) AND (“percutaneous coronary intervention” or “PCI” or “coronary stent implantation”) AND (“aspirin” or “P2Y 12 antagonist” or “P2Y 12 inhibitor” or “clopidogrel” or “ticagrelor” or “warfarin” or “vitamin K antagonist” or “VKA” own “dabigatran” or “rivaroxaban” or “apixaban” or “edoxaban” or “novel oral anticoagulant” or “new oral anticoagulant” or “NOAC”).
Ensure two reviewers perform the search independently.

steps.title: Screen Titles and Abstracts
steps.instruction: Exclude irrelevant studies and non-English language articles based on their titles and abstracts.

steps.title: Perform Full-Text Assessment
steps.instruction: Assess full-text articles to include qualified studies and remove those that do not meet the inclusion/exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Include clinical trials with at least one compared group, patients with paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent AF undergoing PCI, treatment with antiplatelet drugs (aspirin and P2Y12 inhibitors) and/or anticoagulants (warfarin with target INR 2.0-3.0, or NOACs: dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban, edoxaban), outcomes involving MACCEs and major bleeding, and a mean/median follow-up period ≥ 12 months.

Exclude articles published only as abstracts, non-English languages, studies where antithrombotic therapies changed differently post-PCI, vague compared treatments (e.g., VKA vs. non-VAK), and specific article types (clinical trial designs, reviews, meta analyses, letters, case reports, comments, editorials, survey, and investigation).

Exclude studies without a control group, those including non-AF patients undergoing PCI, those with obviously changed treatments in peri-PCI, those without MACCEs or major bleeding endpoints, or those with mean/median follow-up < 1 year.

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Collect specific study and patient data from the qualified studies.

substeps.instruction: Extract study design, sample size (total and per arm), and follow-up duration.
Extract baseline characteristics: mean age, male percentage, mean CHADS 2 /CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc, and HAS-BLED scores.
Extract primary outcome data: number and percentage of MACCEs (all-cause mortality, cardiac death, myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularization, and stroke) at around 1-year follow-up.
Extract secondary outcome data: major bleeding outcomes (defined by TIMI or BARC criteria) at around 1-year follow-up.

steps.title: Assess Study Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality of the included studies using standardized scales.

substeps.instruction: Use the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) for observational studies (evaluating selection, comparability, and outcome).
Use the Jadad Scale for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) (evaluating randomization, double blind, withdrawals, and dropouts).

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the extracted data using Bayesian network meta-analysis.

substeps.instruction: Treat endpoint event results as dichotomous data.
Estimate pooled results using risk ratio (RR) and 95% confidence interval (CI).
Conduct Bayesian network meta-analysis in Addis 1.16.8 software using Markov chain Monte Carlo methods to provide direct/indirect evidence and ranking distribution for the 2 endpoints.

Evaluate inconsistency: if the 95% CI of inconsistency factors median contains 0 and the p-value of the node split model is > 0.05, consider the inconsistent model not significant and proceed with the consistent model.

description: Remove duplicate records by titles and abstracts.
